items.longBusinessSummary: CrowdStrike Holdings, Inc. provides cybersecurity solutions in the United States and internationally. Its unified platform provides cloud-delivered protection of endpoints, cloud workloads, identity, and data through a software as a service (SaaS) subscription-based model. The company offers corporate endpoint and cloud workload security, managed security, security and vulnerability management, IT operations management, identity protection, threat intelligence, data protection, SaaS security posture management, and AI powered workflow automation, and securing generative AI workload services, as well as security orchestration, automation, and response; and security information and event management, and log management services. It primarily sells subscriptions to its Falcon platform and cloud modules. The company has a strategic alliance with Cognizant Technology Solutions Corporation to help enterprises secure artificial intelligence across its lifecycle, from the AI agents and models to the foundational infrastructure that supports the entire AI ecosystem and with Snowflake to bring AI-native security and enterprise data at scale. Additionally, it has a partnership with Fortanix Inc. to combine its Falcon platform with Fortanix Confidential AI to provide an integrated solution for end-to-end AI security. The company was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in Austin, Texas.

Title: Is Crowdstrike’s Rally a Sign of a Sustainable Shift Toward Increased AI Cybersecurity?
Author: Alex Sirois   Tue, October 27, 2026 at 12:15 PM GMT+1 5 min read
Published: 2026-10-27T11:15:06+00:00
=== BODY ===
CRWD surged 14.79% in a week and is up 123% year to date as the AI trade rotates from chip stocks to cybersecurity.
CrowdStrike trades above all 53 analysts' average target of $247, implying 5.6% downside despite 40 Buy or Strong Buy ratings.
Kurtz said the AI DR business "can be bigger than the EDR business" after AIDR ARR nearly tripled versus Q1.
Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and CrowdStrike didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat CRWD. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.
CrowdStrike (NASDAQ:CRWD) trades at $261.83. The AI security boom behind its latest run is real, but that price already reflects much of it. Shares rose 14.79% in a week after Barron's wrote that the AI trade is shifting from chip stocks to cybersecurity.
CrowdStrike sells subscriptions to Falcon, a cloud-native, AI-powered platform that protects endpoints, cloud workloads, identity and data through a single lightweight agent. The stock is up 123.42% year to date. Much of that came from a fiscal second quarter that CEO George Kurtz called "the best quarter in CrowdStrike's history."
Growth is speeding up even at this size. Revenue rose 25.8% to $1.47B, net new ARR jumped 51% to $332.8M, and Falcon Flex ARR topped $2.29B, up 101%. Non-GAAP EPS of $0.31 beat the $0.2915 estimate. That was the company's 9th consecutive beat. Full-year guidance went up to $5.99B to $6.01B in revenue and $1.25 to $1.26 in non-GAAP EPS.
AIDR ending ARR nearly tripled versus Q1, and Kurtz said "the AI DR business can be bigger than the EDR business." Free cash flow came in at $377.4M.
Shares trade at 189x forward earnings and 48.87 times sales. GAAP profit is still thin. Q2 net income was just $5.31M, and GAAP operating income was negative $33.23 million.
24/7 Wall St has helped investors make money for over two decades, and our top analysts just finished ranking the definitive Top 10 Stocks To Buy Now. Not the ten biggest companies. Not the ten everyone is arguing about. The ten best stocks to buy right now.
The report is free, and you can see why we think each stock is a top investment today.
Management's own guidance already shows growth slowing. Q3 net new ARR growth is expected to 29% to 31%, down from Q2's 51%. Costs from the 2024 Falcon outage reached $117.7 million in FY26. Two Sigma, Balyasny and Millennium also cut their stakes in the latest 13F filings.
The business continues to perform well. Retention improved and Q2 closed with a record Q3 pipeline. Even so, the stock already trades above consensus fair value.
The next earnings report will be a key test. Management expected Q3 net new ARR to $343 to $347 million. Beating that range with growth still accelerating would strengthen the bull case. Missing it at this multiple would strengthen the bear case.
CrowdStrike currently trades at $261.83. The average analyst target of $247.25 means about 5.6% downside. Analyst targets offer only a single view, and none of them is a guarantee. Here is how the 53 covering analysts rate the stock:
Shares are up 123.42% year to date. The S&P 500 is up 12.23% over the same period. Over one year, CrowdStrike returned 98.61% against the index's 13%. This past week, the stock rose 14.79% while the S&P 500 slipped 0.15%.
At $261.83, CrowdStrike's valuation already reflects much of its growth.
The shift toward AI security looks durable. Kurtz called it "a sustainable tailwind," and identity ARR increased 34%. But the market already credits much of the raised FY27 outlook.
Net new ARR above $347 million would strengthen the bull case. A result near the low end would suggest the AI jump pulled demand forward. A pullback toward the 50-day moving average of $234.80 would lower the valuation even if the story remains the same.
Momentum could carry shares higher. A sector rotation at 189x forward earnings also carries valuation risk. Every quarter, track net new ARR, Flex ARR, AIDR traction and GAAP operating margin.
CrowdStrike is winning the AI security race, yet this price needs one more quarter of acceleration to support the current valuation.

Title: Black October Is Changing How Companies Buy Cybersecurity. 5 Stocks in the Line of Fire
Author: Trey Thoelcke   Tue, October 27, 2026 at 12:20 PM GMT+1 6 min read
Published: 2026-10-27T11:20:03+00:00
=== BODY ===
Former CISA Director Krebs said 3% of all critical vulnerabilities ever discovered were found in October 2026 alone, triggering a sector-wide patching scramble.
CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz warned smaller companies "don't have the expertise" or money to find vulnerable systems, making them the most exposed targets.
Okta led all five stocks with a 163% year-to-date gain, raising the question of whether Black October tailwinds are already priced in.
Just released. Our analysts combed the entire stock market and named the ten best stocks to buy right now, and CrowdStrike didn't make the cut. Enter your email to see the names that beat CRWD. The report is free. Enter your email and see if any of your stocks made the cut.
In late October 2026, researchers using advanced AI models found critical flaws in PHP, the behind-the-scenes programming language that powers nearly 70% of websites, according to some W3Techs estimates cited by CNBC. A vulnerability is a coding mistake that lets an intruder slip inside. Governments and businesses rushed to patch, and the scramble has been dubbed Black October. Former CISA Director Chris Krebs told CNBC's Squawk Box on Oct. 23 that 3% of all critical vulnerabilities ever discovered had been found in the past month.
Krebs said large companies can use advanced models to secure their systems while small and midsize businesses will struggle, and he urged smaller firms to scan constantly, patch fast, or take legacy systems offline. George Kurtz, the chief executive of CrowdStrike (NASDAQ:CRWD), made the same point on Mad Money on Oct. 26: "The have-nots are the smaller companies that don't have the expertise; they don't have the money behind it. They can't find all of these vulnerable systems that are out there. Those are the systems that I would be worried about."
24/7 Wall St has helped investors make money for over two decades, and our top analysts just finished ranking the definitive Top 10 Stocks To Buy Now. Not the ten biggest companies. Not the ten everyone is arguing about. The ten best stocks to buy right now.
The report is free, and you can see why we think each stock is a top investment today.
Investors moved fast. On October 23, Qualys (NASDAQ:QLYS) rose 3.6%, Tenable (NASDAQ:TENB) 5.1%, Cloudflare (NYSE:NET) 7.1%, CrowdStrike 7.1%, and Okta (NASDAQ:OKTA) 6%, according to StockStory. The ranking below shows how directly the patching scramble feeds each company's core business.
Qualys sells cloud software that scans computers, servers, and cloud accounts for weaknesses and then helps fix them. That makes it the first link in the defense chain. Calculated current billings rose 16% to $176.45 million in the second quarter, up from 8% growth a year earlier. CEO Sumedh Thakar pitched automated patching on the August call: "You cannot solve a minutes problem with a month-long solution." The risk is timing. Thakar described post-Mythos interest as "positive pipeline and dialogue rather than immediate, broad-based spending." Shares trade at $225.15, up 71.9% year to date.
Tenable's Nessus scanner and Tenable One platform map weaknesses across IT, cloud, and industrial systems so teams know what to fix first. Tenable One drove a record 50% of new business in the second quarter, versus 40% a year earlier. CFO Matthew Brown said, "mean time to exploit has compressed over the past year from 30 days to 1.6 days," precisely the vulnerability Black October exposed. However, Co-CEO Mark Thurmond said customers are mainly consolidating onto fewer vendors, which limits fresh budget dollars, and revenue growth slowed to 8.6%. Shares trade at $48.21, up 112.1% year to date.
Cloudflare runs a global network that filters web traffic, blocks DDoS floods, and shields web applications for millions of organizations, a natural shield for unpatched PHP sites. Revenue rose 35.9% to $696.1 million in the second quarter. CFO Thomas Seifert said, "rising cyber risk is more of a demand driver than a negative near-term financial impact." The risk is valuation and profitability: the GAAP net loss grew to $170.0 million on a $150.7 million restructuring charge, and shares trade at 411 times free cash flow. The stock trades at $331.86, up 69.3% year to date.
Okta handles identity and login security, verifying which people and AI agents can access which systems. Current remaining performance obligations rose 14% to $2.58 billion. CFO Brett Tighe cited surveys showing 81% of CISOs know they are exposed to AI agents lacking adequate security. Yet CEO Todd McKinnon said Okta for AI agents is "still too small to show up in the numbers right now." Shares trade at $220.01, up 163.0% year to date, the largest gain here, so much of the benefit may already be priced in.
CrowdStrike's Falcon platform protects laptops, servers, and cloud workloads with a lightweight agent and real-time threat intelligence. Net new ARR rose 51% to $332.8 million. On the August call, management said exposure management sped up, warning that "you simply cannot patch vulnerabilities fast enough." Here's the risk: a $268.1 billion market cap and a 122.7% year-to-date gain set a high bar, as noted in earlier coverage and a report on the coming wave of attacks. Shares trade at $261.83, or 130.9% higher year to date.
Black October shows AI making attacks cheaper and faster, pushing security toward mandatory spending, especially for smaller companies with thin defenses. Scanners like Qualys and Tenable gain most directly, while Cloudflare, Okta, and CrowdStrike serve as the front gate, the lock, and the alarm. The open question is whether a one-time patching scramble turns into lasting budget growth after these stocks already rallied on the news.
If you have cash sitting in your account right now, give this two minutes. After more than two decades of helping investors beat the market, our top analysts at 24/7 Wall St. put together a definitive report on the Top 10 Stocks To Buy Today. And CRWD wasn't one of them.
